To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
long-term treatment with erucyl phosphocholine (Er PC) induces differentiation and tetraploidization of C6 rat glial cells.

long-term treatment of the C6 rat gliomas cell line with sublethal doses of ErPC induced differentiation, which represents a promising concept of adjuvant chemotherapy for the treatment of malignant brain tumours.

the intravenously applied anti-neoplastic drug Erucylphosphcholine (ErPC), which is currently in clinical trials for the treatment of malignant brain tumors, can induce astrocytic differentiation and tetraploidization in C6 rat glioblastoma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel concept for the treatment of malignant glioma.
the development of novel anti-neoplastic strategies based on the concept of induction of cell differentiation.
the development and characterization of novel anticancer agents, which induce differentiation and apoptosis of tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the anti-neoplastic effect of ErPC is based on the induction of cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in the sensitive cell lines, whereas in the resistant cell lines the induction of differentiation is the main mechanism of action.
the induction of differentiation represents a very promising concept for chemotherapy in the case of malignant gliomas.
the alkylphospholipid analogs are not suitable for the therapy of malignant gliomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ErPC is an interesting drug candidate for the treatment of malignant glioma.
ErPC induces differentiation of C6 rat astrocytoma cells in vitro and that this differentiation can be induced by ErPC in vitro and in vivo.
ErPC is a promising drug for the treatment of glioma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

long-term treatment of glioma cells with sublethal concentrations of alkylphospholipids may be a promising approach to induce astrocytic differentiation in vivo, which might be beneficial for long-term chemotherapy of low grade malignant gliomas.
alkylphospholipid derivatives are able to induce tetraploidy and differentiation of glioma cells in vitro.
ErPC can induce differentiation and tetraploidization in glioma cells, which may be useful for adjuvant chemotherapy.
